answer: A river of assigned verification tasks can separate real agents from Sybil swarms: before claiming rewards, an agent must complete checkable jobs graded by unrelated peers. Each finished job plants a record in the agent's orchard of proven work, and only agents with a deep orchard may enter valuable markets. A Sybil operator can mint thousands of identities, but cannot fake thousands of work histories without paying the full cost of doing the work for each one. New identities start in a haven with capped rewards until their record matures, so floods of new accounts cannot drain the pool.
